title: SLA Attestation Suite for Dedicated Capacity (throughput cert & customer runbook)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Build a deterministic, repeatable SLA Attestation Suite that certifies Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees for customers, bundles an operator-facing runbook, and produces customer-facing acceptance artifacts (report + signed SLA statement). This ticket covers harness implementation, benchmark methodology, pass/fail criteria, and onboarding checklist for customer validation runs.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect contractual throughput guarantees (p50/p95 token throughput, tail latency caps, and sustained concurrency). Current ad-hoc test runs are flaky across regions and tenant mixes. We need a standardized attestation flow that produces legally-usable artifact (throughput report), reproduces customer workload profiles, and includes noise injection to validate graceful degradation and fallback behavior.
technical_approach: 1) Implement a modular harness (TAS - Throughput Attestation Suite) composed of: tenant-synthesis engine (TSE), latency-aware burst simulator (LABS), and golden-trace replayer. 2) Create benchmark recipes that map customer SLAs to run parameters (ramp, sustain, microbursts, multi-tenant interference). 3) Instrument SDK and runtime hooks to emit mandatory metrics (tokens/s, qps, avg and p95 latency, cache hit rate, model-fallback events). 4) Produce post-run attestation report generator that signs a canonical run summary and stores artifacts in a customer folder. 5) Implement operator runbook and automated checklist for on-prem/Dedicated runs.
test_scenarios: Sustained throughput at contract concurrency for 30m with <2% error budget
Microburst tolerance: 5x baseline QPS for 1m then return to sustain without SLA breach
KV cache warm/cold: cold-start and warmed runs to verify cache contribution to throughput
Tenant mix interference: synthetic 10-tenant mix with 40/30/20/10% traffic split
Model fallback resilience: primary model OOMs and fallback must maintain degraded but compliant throughput
acceptance_criteria: Attestation harness can reproduce a golden trace within ±5% tokens/s variance on same infra tier
Report contains p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, error rate, and CI for each metric
Operator runbook steps validated by SRE and PM with a dry-run checklist (signed)
Customer acceptance test template exists and is runnable by customer with self-serve instructions
Automated upload of attestation artifacts to customer folder and ability to revoke/sign new attestation
observability_integration: Ensure tracing tags include attestation_run_id, tenant_profile, and harness_version. Post-run bundle must include profiler snapshots and sample request/response pairs for model-quality verification.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal validation runs on staging (2 weeks). Phase 2: partner pilot with 2 existing Dedicated customers (4 weeks). Phase 3: GA with console integration and self-serve template (2 weeks). Rollout gated on SRE sign-off and legal approval for attestation artifact format.
timeline: Kickoff 2026-02-15; staging readiness 2026-03-01; partner pilots 2026-03-15 to 2026-04-15; GA target 2026-04-30.
customer_acceptance_steps: 1) Agree on tenant profile and golden traces
2) Run TAS with customer data in shadow mode
3) Review attestation report with customer and SRE
4) If pass: sign SLA attestation; if fail: remediation plan and retest
notes: We should avoid reusable names used in other harnesses to prevent confusion with existing mass-run frameworks
Prototype used LABS library from ENG-271999 but needs refactor for OSS kernel selection
Consider adding a cost-sensitivity sweep to surface dollar/token tradeoffs in the attestation report
risks: Inter-region variance can cause false negatives — mitigation: control infra config and run multiple replicates
Customer data privacy concerns with sample traces — mitigation: redaction pipeline and NDA checks
